title: Cyrus and the Cipher
premise: Mirabel Almeida, a retired detective whose failing bookshop is his last refuge, receives two letters from the same hand: one confessing to a thirty-year-old murder, the other promising the truth if he can find it first. The dead man is Cyrus Okonkwo, the partner whose betrayal ended Mirabel's career, and the letters force him to confront the alibi he built — and lied about — all those years ago. As Mirabel follows a cipher hidden in Cyrus's old case notes through Lagos's forgotten archives and its living witnesses, he discovers his own testimony was the linchpin of the cover-up. In the end, Mirabel must choose between protecting the person who has loyally protected him for decades and publishing the truth that will destroy them both; he chooses truth, closes the case at last, and reopens the bookshop under a new name.
about_author: August Oyelaran is a former court clerk from Ibadan who spent fifteen years transcribing testimonies before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. A slow week at Almeida's Books ends when two letters arrive in identical handwriting: one confessing to Cyrus Okonkwo's murder, one promising 'the rest' if Mirabel can find where the confession lies. The emotional beat is reluctant awakening — Mirabel recognizes the handwriting instantly and feels thirty years collapse.

chapters.title: The Alibi I Built
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel, with flashbacks. Mirabel rereads his own 1994 case file and confronts the testimony he fabricated to protect someone unnamed. His daughter Adaeze notices him pulling old boxes from the cellar. The beat is guilt resurfacing; the reader learns Mirabel's celebrated final case rests on a lie.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Deciphering numbers tucked into Cyrus's donated notebooks, Mirabel finds references to a warehouse fire never officially investigated. He visits retired Inspector Bello, who warns him off with genuine fear. Beat: the thrill of pursuit shadowed by dread — someone else is asking the same questions.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Forgot
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mirabel and an elderly witness, Mama Ejiro. She claims to remember nothing about the fire until Mirabel mentions Cyrus's name, then recites details only an eyewitness could know — then begs him to leave. Beat: the past is not buried; it is guarded.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Questions
chapters.summary: POV: Adaeze. Mirabel's daughter, who manages the bookshop accounts, finds the letters and demands answers. Their confrontation reveals how much she sacrificed for his reputation. Beat: loyalty as inheritance — she threatens to burn the letters to protect him, echoing his own old choice.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. A third letter arrives, naming the writer: Tunde, Mirabel's former junior officer and oldest friend. It admits Tunde falsified evidence on Cyrus's orders — and implies Cyrus was killed for what he knew about the fire. Beat: betrayal reframed; the man Mirabel protected may be the murderer's accomplice or victim.

chapters.title: Warehouse Ashes
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Following the cipher to the ruined warehouse, Mirabel finds a hidden strongbox containing documents proving the fire was arson committed by a now-powerful businessman, and that Cyrus was blackmailing him. Beat: vertigo — every ally in the old case had a price, including Cyrus himself.

chapters.title: What Tunde Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Tunde. Dying of illness, Tunde confesses fully: he wrote both letters to force Mirabel to finish what fear made him abandon. But he also reveals the final cipher layer points to someone still alive who saw the killing. Beat: grief and urgency — time is running out because Tunde's doctors are running out.

chapters.title: The Last Witness
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The trail leads to Mama Ejiro again — she saw the businessman's fixer kill Cyrus but stayed silent to protect her son, whom the fixer blackmailed. The businessman's men close in on the bookshop. Beat: climax — Mirabel must trade his silence, the thing he built his life on, for her testimony.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel hands everything to a journalist and a prosecutor, sacrificing his name and Tunde's legacy to the truth; the businessman falls, Mama Ejiro's son is spared prosecution, and Tunde dies knowing the record is set straight. Mirabel repaints the shop sign: 'Almeida & Okonkwo.' Beat: costly peace — identity rebuilt on honesty rather than legend.
